newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. insurer John Hancock plans China venture.
newsitem.headline: U.S. insurer John Hancock plans China venture.

text.p: U.S.-based John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Co plans to establish a joint venture to sell life insurance in China within the next three years, a company official said on Monday.

"We would hope to have a joint venture operating here in China within the next three years," said Lance Tay, assistant vice president for business development of John Hancock International Services Pte Ltd in Singapore.

"We are actively looking at local insurance companies as our potential partners," Tay said in an interview, adding that the venture was likely to be based in Shanghai or the southern city of Guangzhou.
"There's a lot of room (for newcomers) because this is a new market," Tay said.
"Shanghai has 15 million people with almost zero penetration for individual life insurance," he said.
Beijing has said it would gradually allow more foreign insurance firms to set up shop in China as part of its bid to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

Competition to win those coveted licences to sell insurance in China is sharp, and dozens of the world's top insurers are lining up for the chance to flog their products to the world's most populated country.
Tay said Beijing had granted licences to just a handful of foreign insurers to sell their products in China with only two foreign backed companies currently selling life insurance.

American International Assurance Co Ltd -- a member company of the American International Group -- and a joint venture between Canada's Manulife Financial and a financial firm under Chinese state company Sinochem now sell life insurance in China.
Before 1993, the life insurance market in China was dominated by three domestic companies -- the People's Insurance Co of China (PICC), China Pacific Insurance Co and Ping An Insurance Co, he said.

"Prior to 1993, when the first foreign life insurance company arrived in China, life insurance was sold as group insurance to the employer," Tay said. "It was not the life insurance sold door-to-door to individuals."
Foreign life insurance firms could offer more flexible policies, better service and a greater variety of products than China's domestic insurers, he said.
John Hancock was established in the United States in 1862 and is one of the world's largest life insurance companies, with assets under its management now exceeding $100 billion, the company says.
Tay said the company already had representative offices in Shanghai, Beijing and Tianjin and was awaiting approval for a fourth in Guangzhou.
